designSummary.target: src/jobs/parcel-r5-zoning.mjs's processCity / RESIDUE_HAS_REAL_ZONING_SQL / loadResidueWithRealZoning, plus a new revisit flag in src/config/zoning-layer-completeness.mjs.
designSummary.theHole: CTX-PARCELGATE's condition 2 correctly excludes a residual parcel from the refused sweep when it already carries a real zoning_district in txgio_parcel elsewhere (the staleness class: 17 Bastrop / 50 Travis, both re-verified live). But nothing else in this rail ever writes that parcel a value -- it matched no polygon in this rail's own spatial join, which is the only other path to 'value'. Two prior closes (CTX-ZONESCOPE, CTX-PARCELGATE) assumed a 'pending Factory re-bake' would resolve these parcels to value on its own. Traced and confirmed that job does not exist -- not deferred, not scheduled, fabricated by inference and repeated. Per the dispatch, not chasing it further.
designSummary.theFix: When a residual parcel is condition-2-eligible (a real txgio_parcel.zoning_district exists elsewhere), write it a value cell instead of leaving it unaccounted. Source must NOT be ZONING_SOURCE (tx_zoning_district_staging) -- that value never came from there; a new STAMP_SOURCE constant names the actual origin (legacy-design-tools' stampCountyZoning(), from its own zoning-layers.ts registry, confirmed by direct read of zoning-stamp-db.ts's UPDATE statement).
designSummary.reuseDesign: Per the dispatch's explicit instruction ('one definition, two consumers... two independent queries that must agree would drift'): RESIDUE_HAS_REAL_ZONING_SQL's EXISTS gate stays byte-for-byte the eligibility decision (unchanged predicate, still EXISTS, still never a flat join -- the existing pinned SQL-shape test enforces this). Widened via three correlated scalar subqueries (same predicate, LIMIT 1 by feature_index) to also return the value in the SAME round trip, rather than adding a second, independently-derived query. loadResidueWithRealZoning's return type changes from Set<string> to Map<string, {districtCode, jurisdiction, ingestedAt}> -- membership (.has, condition 2's original use) and value (.get, this card's new use) come from one query result.
designSummary.currencyPlan: Checked the schema (txgioParcel.ts) and the write path (zoning-stamp-db.ts, zoning-cli.ts): no stamp-date column exists anywhere, and the CLI persists no audit/run log (only console.log). Found one real, derivable lower bound instead: legacy-design-tools' geometry-ingest CLI wholesale-replaces a county's txgio_parcel rows (DELETE then a fresh INSERT whose column list excludes zoning_district -- confirmed in ingest.ts's replaceCountyParcels/upsertTxgioParcels), so a currently non-null zoning_district proves the stamp ran strictly after that row's own ingested_at. Plan: carry ingested_at as stampProvenance.currencyFloor with an honest currencyNote stating it is a lower bound, never an exact stamp date. To be live-verified at CP2 against the actual 17/50 population before committing to this as sufficient.
designSummary.revisitFlagPlan: ZONING_REGISTRY_RECONCILIATION_DEFERRED, a frozen object in src/config/zoning-layer-completeness.mjs (co-located with the sibling PER_COUNTY_CEILING_INSTRUMENT_DEFERRED flag from CTX-PARCELGATE, same shape: deferred/deferredWhy/ruledBy/revisitTriggers, plus a required fallbackCost field per this dispatch's explicit ask). Names: what is deferred (reconciling hauska-engine's zoning-staging registry against legacy-design-tools' zoning-layers registry), why (unblock the Central Texas bake, operator ruling 2026-09-09), what this fallback costs (a value whose provenance is a second registry the staged layer disagrees with -- honest, not the same claim as coverage), what triggers a revisit. Pinned by a dedicated test, same pattern as the sibling flag.
